function: p. 4, 7: Predicts the optimal beam index (64-beam codebook) at the RSU from camera, LiDAR, radar and GPS using a hierarchical Transformer fusion network.
system: p. 3, 11: RSU with a uniform linear array, 64-beam codebook, camera, LiDAR, radar and GPS; vehicle with omnidirectional mmWave transmitters (DeepSense 6G scenarios 31-34); no RIS.
method: p. 5-10: Supervised (focal loss on beam labels) hierarchical Transformer fusion over ResNet branches; KL-importance structured pruning with fine-tuning; conditional VAE trained separately to generate missing modality features.
data_channel: p. 11: Public measured DeepSense 6G scenarios 31-34 (urban street, day and night), 11,243 samples; 10,118 for training and 1,125 for validation.
test_conditions: p. 11, 13: 90/10 train-validation split of the pooled scenarios 31-34; separate test with one modality zero-filled, noise-filled or CVAE-generated, without retraining BeamTransFuser.
baselines: p. 11-13: Beam prediction vs learned Avatar, [11] position-based and multi-modal, TII, CMDF, QTNs, ICMFE, MMDL, MMT (no non-learned beam search); missing modality vs zero-fill, noise, modality dropout.
metrics: p. 11, 13: DBA-Score and Top-k accuracy; also parameter count, inference latency on three GPUs, and CVAE latency overhead.
complexity: p. 12-13: 78.42 million parameters; pruning to remaining ratio 0.4-1.0; inference latency measured on GTX 1080, RTX 4070Ti and L20; CVAE adds about 17 ms.
openness: p. 11: No code released by the authors; trains and tests on the public DeepSense 6G dataset [23], challenge page deepsense6g.net in ref. [26].
q1_support: p. 11: "multi-modal data collected from real-world vehicular communication scenarios" (DeepSense 6G scenarios 31-34, measured data used for training and validation).
q2_support: p. 13: "The corrupted inputs are then fed into BeamTransFuser for inference." BeamTransFuser, trained on all four modalities, is tested with one modality zero-filled, noise-filled or CVAE-generated, without retraining (p. 3: "conditions without requiring re-training"); the 90/10 split of pooled scenarios (p. 11) is held-out data of the same dataset and is not counted.
q3_support: p. 11: "We include all existing methods that utilize" the same dataset: all learned beam predictors (Avatar, [11], TII, CMDF, QTNs, ICMFE, MMDL, MMT) on DBA-Score and Top-k (Tables III-IV); no non-learned beam-selection baseline; zero-filled and noise replacement (p. 13) run the same network with degraded input.
q4_support: p. 13: "We further evaluate the inference latency across three hardware platforms" and "the additional overhead of CVAE-based completion is" 17.11 ms; model size 78.42 million parameters (Table II, p. 8).
q5_support: p. 11: "We utilize the DeepSense 6G dataset [23] to" evaluate beam prediction, and "As a publicly available and widely" used multi-modal dataset; the authors release no code of their own.
notes: Area 5 because the paper frames the system as ISAC (p. 1, 3) and beamforming in an ISAC system is area 5; by function (beam index prediction for communication, sensing only as input) area 3 is the alternative. q2 borderline: counted on the missing-modality tests, since the 90/10 split is held-out data of the same pooled scenarios. q3=0 because every compared beam predictor is learned; if the reviewer accepts zero-filled/noise replacement and modality dropout (Table V, p. 13) as baselines for the generative module, q3 would be 1.
